sample_unit: young adults (ages 18 to 32) completing a guided chatbot interaction and survey
models_evaluated: Roo (Planned Parenthood Federation of America sexual and reproductive health chatbot)

links.outcome: Differences in chatbot adoption intention and readiness across education and income bands
links.effect: Adoption intention gradient absent (d = -.09). Readiness gradients small (d between -.15 and -.24). Education and income correlations with the nine adoption constructs at or below .09. No demographic group showed an adoption penalty.
links.quote: Conditional on digital inclusion, the chatbot’s front door opened equally.

unlisted_practices: Teaching chatbot-specific eHealth literacy as a way to narrow socioeconomic gaps in adoption

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating user adoption, equity, and interaction dynamics of an AI chatbot (Roo by Planned Parenthood) among diverse socioeconomic groups of young adults using guided interactions and surveys.
